artists.biography: Richard Barbieri has been Porcupine Tree's keyboard/synthesizer player since 1993 (what started as a studio/home project by Steven Wilson developed into a successful touring band with major label releases and a worldwide profile).  Richard's musical career started at the age of 17 when he joined the band Japan. During the early eighties the band achieved commercial and critical success culminating in the groundbreaking album Tin Drum which stayed in the album charts for a year. The album sessions involved Richard in his most intense period of analogue synthesizer programming.  More recently, Richard began to leave the "comfort zone" of his analogue synthesizers in favour of exploring the potential offered by digital synthesizers. His debut solo album Things Buried was released in 2005. He has also been involved in a number of projects with former Japan bandmates David Sylvian, Mick Karn, and Steve Jansen in various combinations, including Rain Tree Crow (which was a full Japan reunion).

perplexity.description:
Planets + Persona is Richard Barbieri's third solo album, released in 2017 on the Kscope label. The album showcases a blend of progressive electronic and rock elements, featuring extended instrumental compositions that highlight Barbieri's distinctive keyboard work. Tracks like "Solar Sea," "Night Of The Hunter," and "Interstellar Medium" demonstrate his approach to post-progressive music, with pieces ranging from nearly eleven minutes to under six minutes in length. The album's thematic framework, suggested by its title, explores the intersection of cosmic imagery and personal introspection through its sonic landscape.

Within Barbieri's solo career, Planets + Persona represents a significant statement following his earlier albums Things Buried (2004/5) and Stranger Inside (2008). The release established his continued commitment to expansive, compositionally ambitious work outside his primary roles with Porcupine Tree and Japan. The album's placement on Kscope, a label dedicated to post-progressive and boundary-pushing music, aligned Barbieri with a community of artists exploring similar sonic territories.

The album received recognition within progressive music circles as a solid entry in the post-progressive genre, appealing to listeners of contemporary instrumental rock and electronic music. Its release on Kscope positioned it within the label's catalog of adventurous releases, and the album has maintained presence through subsequent vinyl and digital reissues, indicating sustained interest among progressive music audiences.
